title: Genesis Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 7.

questions.question: Who did the LORD command to come into the ark?
questions.correctAnswer: Noah and all his house
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:1 states that the LORD said unto Noah, "Come thou and all thy house into the ark."

questions.question: How many of every clean beast was Noah commanded to take into the ark?
options: Seven, the male and his female
Two, the male and his female
Five, the male and his female
Ten, the male and his female
questions.correctAnswer: Seven, the male and his female
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:2 instructs Noah to take of every clean beast by sevens, the male and his female.

questions.question: How many of the beasts that are not clean did Noah take into the ark?
options: Two, the male and his female
Seven, the male and his female
Ten, the male and his female
questions.correctAnswer: Two, the male and his female
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:2 says for beasts that are not clean, Noah was to take two, the male and his female.

questions.question: What purpose was given for taking seven of the fowls of the air?
options: To keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth
To fill the ark with noise
questions.correctAnswer: To keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:3 states that seven of the fowls were taken to keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth.

questions.question: How many days did the LORD say it would rain upon the earth?
questions.correctAnswer: Forty days and forty nights
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:4 says the LORD will cause it to rain forty days and forty nights.

questions.question: Did Noah obey all the commandments given by the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:5 states that Noah did according unto all that the LORD commanded him.

questions.question: How old was Noah when the flood of waters was upon the earth?
questions.correctAnswer: Six hundred years old
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:6 declares that Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters was upon the earth.

questions.question: Who entered the ark because of the waters of the flood?
options: Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives
questions.correctAnswer: Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:7 states that Noah went in, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him, into the ark.

questions.question: True or False: The animals that entered the ark included only clean beasts.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:8 mentions clean beasts, beasts that are not clean, fowls, and everything that creepeth upon the earth entered the ark.

questions.question: The animals entered the ark in what manner?
options: Two and two, male and female
questions.correctAnswer: Two and two, male and female
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:9 states that there went in two and two unto Noah into the ark, the male and the female.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD shut Noah in the ark after all went in.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:16 states that after they went in, the LORD shut him in.

questions.question: What was the length of time the flood waters prevailed upon the earth?
questions.correctAnswer: One hundred and fifty days
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:24 reports that the waters prevailed upon the earth one hundred and fifty days.

questions.question: In Genesis 7, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Come thou and all thy house into the ark
Take seven of every clean beast
Wait seven days before the rain
questions.correctAnswer: Come thou and all thy house into the ark
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:1 contains the first command: to come into the ark with all his house, before instructions about animals or waiting.

questions.question: True or False: The flood covered all the high hills under the whole heaven.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:19 states that all the high hills under the whole heaven were covered by the waters.

questions.question: What happened on the seventeenth day of the second month in Noah's six hundredth year?
options: All the fountains of the great deep were broken up and the windows of heaven were opened
questions.correctAnswer: All the fountains of the great deep were broken up and the windows of heaven were opened
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:11 describes that on that day the fountains of the great deep broke up and the windows of heaven opened.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Genesis 7:9, how did the animals enter the ark?
options: Two and two, male and female
questions.correctAnswer: Two and two, male and female
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:9 states that animals went into the ark two and two, male and female, as God commanded Noah. This shows God's command for pairs to preserve life.

questions.question: How many days passed after the animals entered the ark before the floodwaters came upon the earth?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:10 explains that after seven days, the waters of the flood were upon the earth, connecting the waiting period after the animals entered the ark.

questions.question: What significant event happened on the seventeenth day of the second month in Noah's six hundredth year?
options: Noah received instructions to build the ark
The fountains of the great deep were broken up and the windows of heaven opened
The rain stopped after forty days
The ark came to rest on a mountain
questions.correctAnswer: The fountains of the great deep were broken up and the windows of heaven opened
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:11 states that on this day, the fountains of the great deep were broken up and the windows of heaven opened, initiating the flood.

questions.question: For how long did the rain fall upon the earth according to Genesis 7:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Forty days and forty nights
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:12 records that the rain lasted forty days and forty nights, marking the duration of the flood's initial precipitation.

questions.question: Who entered the ark on the same day as Noah according to Genesis 7:13?
options: Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives
Noah, his sons, and their children
questions.correctAnswer: Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:13 specifies that Noah, his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, his wife, and the three wives of his sons entered the ark the same day.

questions.question: What does Genesis 7:14 emphasize about the variety of creatures that entered the ark?
options: Only birds and creeping things were taken
Every beast, cattle, creeping thing, and fowl after their kind
questions.correctAnswer: Every beast, cattle, creeping thing, and fowl after their kind
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:14 highlights the inclusion of every beast, cattle, creeping thing, and bird after their kind, showing God's provision for all living creatures.

questions.question: According to Genesis 7:15, how many of each kind of living creature entered the ark?
options: Two and two of all flesh
Seven pairs of clean animals only
questions.correctAnswer: Two and two of all flesh
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:15 confirms that two and two of all flesh, meaning pairs, entered the ark to preserve life.

questions.question: What action did the LORD take after all beings entered the ark according to Genesis 7:16?
options: He shut Noah and those with him in the ark
He caused the animals to multiply
questions.correctAnswer: He shut Noah and those with him in the ark
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:16 states that after all went in, the LORD shut Noah and those inside the ark in, demonstrating divine protection and finality.

questions.question: How does Genesis 7:15–16 teach us about obedience and trust in God?
options: Obedience is optional, and trust is uncertain
Obedience to God's command leads to protection, showing trust in His provision
God commands but does not intervene
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's command leads to protection, showing trust in His provision
questions.explanation: Verses 15 and 16 show that Noah obeyed God's instructions fully, entering the ark with all creatures and being shut in by God, illustrating trust and obedience leading to divine protection.

questions.question: What does Genesis 7:11-12 teach about the certainty of God's judgment following obedience to His commands?
options: God's judgment comes in His appointed time after obedience
Judgment is not related to obedience
God's judgment is immediate and instantaneous
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment comes in His appointed time after obedience
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:11-12 shows that after Noah obeyed God's command to enter the ark, the flood began exactly on the appointed day, indicating God's judgment follows His timing after obedience.

questions.question: How can Genesis 7:13 inspire humility in believers facing difficult circumstances?
options: By encouraging pride in one's strength
By showing reliance on God’s provision and protection through obedience
By downplaying the severity of trials
questions.correctAnswer: By showing reliance on God’s provision and protection through obedience
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:13 shows Noah and his family entering the ark as God commanded, reminding believers to humbly rely on God's provision during trials.

questions.question: A friend is struggling with trusting God's timing during hardship. Based on Genesis 7:10-12, what biblical truth could you share?
options: God's promises are immediate and always visible
God’s timing is perfect; after waiting seven days, the flood began exactly as God said
Human timing is more reliable than God's
questions.correctAnswer: God’s timing is perfect; after waiting seven days, the flood began exactly as God said
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:10-12 emphasize that after Noah's obedience and a seven-day wait, the flood began precisely when God declared, teaching trust in God's perfect timing.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 7:14, only clean animals entered the ark.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:14 states that every beast, cattle, creeping thing, and fowl after their kind entered the ark, not just clean animals.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 7:9 teaches that God commands obedience through specific instructions, such as bringing animals in pairs into the ark.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:9 shows that God commanded Noah to bring animals two and two, male and female, demonstrating specific instructions requiring obedience.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 7:16 indicates that after Noah and the animals entered, the ark remained open for others to enter later.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:16 states that after all entered, the LORD shut Noah in the ark, indicating it was closed and no one else could enter later.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 7.

questions.question: How long did the floodwaters prevail upon the earth according to Genesis 7?
questions.correctAnswer: One hundred and fifty days
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:24 states that the waters prevailed upon the earth for one hundred and fifty days, indicating the total duration of the floodwaters covering the earth.

questions.question: What happened to the ark as the waters increased during the flood?
options: It was lifted up above the earth
questions.correctAnswer: It was lifted up above the earth
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:17 describes that the waters increased and bore up the ark, lifting it above the earth, emphasizing God's protection over Noah's vessel.

questions.question: According to Genesis 7, what covered the high hills under the whole heaven?
questions.correctAnswer: Water
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:19 states that the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth and covered all the high hills under the whole heaven, symbolizing the complete inundation of the earth.

questions.question: How far upward did the waters prevail, covering the mountains?
questions.correctAnswer: Fifteen cubits
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:20 specifies that the waters prevailed fifteen cubits upward, covering the mountains, indicating the depth of the floodwaters above the highest elevations.

questions.question: What happened to all flesh that moved upon the earth during the flood?
options: They were saved by the ark
questions.correctAnswer: They died
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:21 clearly states that all flesh that moved upon the earth, including birds, cattle, beasts, creeping things, and every man, died during the flood.

questions.question: Which phrase in Genesis 7:22 emphasizes the totality of death during the flood?
options: "All in whose nostrils was the breath of life died"
questions.correctAnswer: "All in whose nostrils was the breath of life died"
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:22 emphasizes the complete destruction by stating that all living beings with the breath of life in their nostrils died, underlining the comprehensive nature of the flood.

questions.question: Who were the only survivors of the flood according to Genesis 7?
options: All the animals except unclean beasts
questions.correctAnswer: Noah and his family
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:23 states that every living substance was destroyed except Noah and those with him in the ark, indicating their unique preservation.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God's judgment by water as seen in Genesis 7?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 54:9
questions.explanation: Isaiah 54:9 references the floodwaters as a symbol of God's judgment and covenant, connecting directly to Genesis 7's flood narrative.

questions.question: What literary device is employed in Genesis 7:19-20 when describing the waters covering the hills and mountains?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:19-20 uses parallelism by repeating the theme of waters prevailing and covering high elevations, a common Hebrew poetic structure.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word translated as "prevailed" in Genesis 7:18 regarding the floodwaters?
options: It means 'to overcome or be mighty'
questions.correctAnswer: It means 'to overcome or be mighty'
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'radah' translated as 'prevailed' conveys the idea of being mighty or having dominion, emphasizing the overwhelming power of the floodwaters in Genesis 7:18.

questions.question: How does the flood narrative in Genesis 7 foreshadow New Testament baptism themes?
options: By illustrating water as cleansing from sin
questions.correctAnswer: By illustrating water as cleansing from sin
questions.explanation: The flood represents judgment and cleansing, prefiguring baptism's symbolism of death to sin and new life, as echoed in 1 Peter 3:20-21, connecting to Genesis 7's cleansing waters.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 7 states that only clean animals were brought into the ark in sevens to keep their seed alive.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:2-3 distinguishes between clean animals taken by sevens and unclean by twos, but Genesis 7:9-15 emphasize two by two for all flesh entering the ark, not only clean animals in sevens.

questions.question: True or False: The windows of heaven were opened on the seventeenth day of the second month in Noah's six hundredth year, starting the flood.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:11 states that on that exact day, the fountains of the great deep were broken up and the windows of heaven opened, initiating the flood.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage references the flood in Genesis 7 as a typology for salvation through water?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 3:20-21 explicitly references Noah's flood as a typology for baptism and salvation, connecting to the Genesis 7 flood narrative.

questions.question: What cultural significance did the flood narrative in Genesis 7 have for the ancient Near Eastern audience?
options: It demonstrated the superiority of the Hebrew God over other gods
It was a historical record of trade routes
It described the origins of the alphabet
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrated the superiority of the Hebrew God over other gods
questions.explanation: The flood story highlighted God's judgment and control over creation, contrasting with polytheistic flood myths in the ancient Near East, asserting the Hebrew God's supremacy.

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Genesis 7:1 reveal about God's judgment and grace toward Noah?
options: God saw Noah as righteous in a corrupt generation and called him and his household into the ark
God judged Noah as sinful but spared him for his family
God ignored Noah's righteousness and judged all equally
God saved only Noah, not his family
questions.correctAnswer: God saw Noah as righteous in a corrupt generation and called him and his household into the ark
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:1 shows that God recognized Noah's righteousness in his generation, which motivated God to command Noah and his household to enter the ark, demonstrating divine grace toward the righteous amid judgment.

questions.question: According to Genesis 7:2, what does the specific number of clean animals to be taken signify in God's covenantal provision?
options: Seven pairs of clean animals symbolize completeness and preservation
Only one pair of clean animals was needed
Clean animals were not required on the ark
Twelve pairs of clean animals represented the tribes of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Seven pairs of clean animals symbolize completeness and preservation
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:2 prescribes seven pairs of clean animals, indicating God's thorough provision for preserving species necessary for sacrificial purposes and covenant continuity, symbolizing divine completeness.

questions.question: How does Genesis 7:4 demonstrate God's attribute of justice in relation to creation?
options: God declares He will destroy every living substance due to universal corruption
God shows mercy by sparing all creatures
God is indifferent to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: God declares He will destroy every living substance due to universal corruption
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:4 reveals God's justice in response to pervasive sinfulness, as He plans to destroy every living substance on earth, underscoring the seriousness of divine judgment upon a corrupt creation.

questions.question: What theological significance does Noah's obedience in Genesis 7:5 have in the doctrine of sanctification?
options: It exemplifies faithful submission to God's commands as a form of holiness
It shows human works alone save from judgment
It emphasizes human wisdom over divine instruction
It indicates reluctance to obey God
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies faithful submission to God's commands as a form of holiness
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:5 highlights Noah's obedience to God's commands, illustrating sanctification as faithful response and holiness in action, aligning with the biblical teaching of living by faith and obedience.

questions.question: What does the precise timing in Genesis 7:11 (six hundredth year, second month, seventeenth day) reveal about God's providence?
options: God sovereignly controls the unfolding of redemptive history with exact timing
The timing is incidental and holds no significance
The flood was delayed due to human repentance
The date reflects an astrological event
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly controls the unfolding of redemptive history with exact timing
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:11's exact dating demonstrates God's providential sovereignty in executing judgment and salvation within His redemptive plan, showing that God's timing governs human history.

questions.question: How does the inclusion of Noah's sons and their wives in Genesis 7:7 contribute to the doctrine of covenant community?
options: It affirms the preservation of a covenant family representing humanity's continuation
It suggests only Noah was righteous, others were saved by chance
It excludes women from God's redemptive plan
It implies salvation was limited to Noah alone
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms the preservation of a covenant family representing humanity's continuation
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:7 shows that Noah's family entered the ark together, emphasizing God's covenantal preservation of a family unit to continue human life and fulfill divine promises.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the LORD shut him in' in Genesis 7:16 reveal about God's attribute?
options: God's sovereign protection and control over salvation
God's abandonment of Noah and the ark
Human effort alone secured the ark's safety
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereign protection and control over salvation
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:16 indicates that God Himself secured Noah in the ark, symbolizing divine sovereignty and protection in the work of salvation, a key attribute of God as protector and preserver.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is taught by the flood waters prevailing and lifting the ark above the earth as described in Genesis 7:17?
options: God's judgment is both overwhelming and redemptive, lifting the ark as a means of salvation
The flood was a minor event with no theological impact
The ark sank beneath the waters indicating failure
Water symbolized chaos without divine involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is both overwhelming and redemptive, lifting the ark as a means of salvation
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:17 teaches that while God's judgment through the flood is comprehensive and devastating, it also provides salvation by lifting the ark above destruction, foreshadowing redemptive deliverance.

questions.question: How does Genesis 7:19-20's description of the waters covering the mountains connect to the universal scope of God's judgment?
options: It illustrates that God's judgment was worldwide, affecting all creation
It suggests judgment was localized only to certain regions
It implies mountains were spared from the flood
It shows the flood was symbolic, not literal
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates that God's judgment was worldwide, affecting all creation
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:19-20 emphasizes the flood's comprehensive nature by stating that all high hills and mountains were covered, confirming the universal extent of divine judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Genesis 7:21-22 provide regarding the consequence of sin on all living beings?
options: Sin brought universal death to all flesh breathing life on dry land
Only humans were judged; animals were spared
Sin had no effect on creation
questions.correctAnswer: Sin brought universal death to all flesh breathing life on dry land
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:21-22 teach that the flood resulted in the death of all living creatures with the breath of life on dry land, revealing sin's devastating and comprehensive impact on creation.

questions.question: What theological meaning does the phrase 'only Noah remained alive' in Genesis 7:23 hold in the context of salvation history?
options: Noah is a type of the faithful remnant preserved by God through judgment
Noah was the sole righteous man ever
Salvation was based on works apart from God's grace
questions.correctAnswer: Noah is a type of the faithful remnant preserved by God through judgment
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:23 shows that only Noah and those with him survived, symbolizing God's preservation of a faithful remnant, a key theme in salvation history reflecting divine mercy amid judgment.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the flood narrative is mythological and lacks historical basis. What does Genesis 7:24 teach about the duration and reality of the flood event?
options: The waters prevailed for 150 days, indicating a prolonged, real judgment event
The flood lasted only a few hours, suggesting myth
No specific duration is given, supporting a legend
The flood was symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: The waters prevailed for 150 days, indicating a prolonged, real judgment event
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:24 specifies the flood lasting 150 days, supporting the historicity and seriousness of the event as a real divine judgment rather than myth, affirming biblical reliability (cf. 2 Peter 3:6).

questions.question: What combined theological truth is taught by Genesis 7:3 and Genesis 7:15 about God's purpose in preserving animal life?
options: God preserves seed and breath of life to ensure continuity of creation
Animals were not preserved during the flood
Only clean animals were saved for sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves seed and breath of life to ensure continuity of creation
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:3 and 7:15 together teach that God intentionally preserves pairs of animals and the breath of life to maintain life on earth, demonstrating His providential care over creation's continuity.

questions.question: What theological significance does the breaking up of 'the fountains of the great deep' and the opening of the 'windows of heaven' in Genesis 7:11 have regarding God's control over creation?
options: It reveals God's sovereign control over both subterranean and celestial waters in judgment
It suggests natural forces acted independently of God
It indicates chaos escaped God's control
It shows God was powerless over the flood
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals God's sovereign control over both subterranean and celestial waters in judgment
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:11 illustrates God's authority over all elements of creation, including waters below and above, affirming His sovereign judgment and control in executing the flood.

questions.question: How does Genesis 7:8 demonstrate the inclusiveness of God's judgment and mercy toward all earth's creatures?
options: All creatures—clean, unclean, fowls, and creeping things—were included in the flood judgment and preservation plan
Only humans were judged, animals excluded
Some animals were exempt from judgment
questions.correctAnswer: All creatures—clean, unclean, fowls, and creeping things—were included in the flood judgment and preservation plan
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:8 shows God's judgment encompassed every kind of living creature, yet His mercy included preserving representatives of all kinds, highlighting His comprehensive justice and grace.
